title: Kernel-based External Validity of Experimental Studies
abstract: arXiv:2610.13625v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The external validity of a study is the extent to which its findings generalize to unseen experimental conditions, such as datasets. We formalize the results of a study together with its research question, and define external validity as the probability that two independent and same-sized replications of the study produce results whose maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) is below a given tolerance. This approach, centered on the choice of a space of results and of an appropriate reproducing kernel for the MMD, is flexible enough to be deployed on multiple different types of results and research questions. Additionally, we establish an asymptotic power-law relation between the size of a study and the quantiles of the MMD, which we use to estimate the desired size of an externally valid study from a small-scale preliminary study. We deploy our framework to rankings with ties and discuss kernels suited to different research questions. Experime

translated_title: 基于核方法的实验研究外部有效性
translated_abstract: 一项研究的外部有效性是指其研究结果能够泛化到未见过的实验条件（如数据集）的程度。我们将研究结果及其研究问题共同形式化，并将外部有效性定义为：该研究的两次独立且规模相同的重复实验所产生的结果之间的最大均值差异（MMD）低于给定容差的概率。这一方法以结果空间的选择以及适用于MMD的合适再生核为核心，足够灵活，可应用于多种不同类型的结果和研究问题。此外，我们建立了研究规模与MMD分位数之间的渐近幂律关系，并利用该关系从小规模的初步研究中估计出具有外部有效性的研究所需的规模。我们将该框架应用于带并列的排名问题，并讨论了适合不同研究问题的核函数。
tldr: 该论文提出用核方法（最大均值差异MMD）形式化定义实验研究的外部有效性，并建立了研究规模与MMD分位数之间的渐近幂律关系，从而能够从小规模初步研究估计出具有外部有效性的研究所需规模。
en_tdlr: The paper formalizes the external validity of experimental studies using kernel methods (maximum mean discrepancy, MMD) and establishes an asymptotic power-law relation between study size and MMD quantiles, enabling estimation of the required size of an externally valid study from a small-scale preliminary study.
